description: Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(size of its Murcko scaffold family within the training fold, normalised to mean 1), applied to the random forest and LightGBM base learners only.

The job timed out because each fit ran the full stacking pipeline (5 outer folds x an inner 4-fold KRR grid search of 9 configs, plus a final base fit), which is far too slow for 15 fits in 600 s; I drop the nested OOF stacking and the KRR grid search, and average the three base learners directly.

Replace the stack's Ridge(alpha=1e-3, positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative L1 (least-absolute-deviation) fit solved by scipy linprog (HiGHS), with no intercept, and apply the resulting weights to the base-learner test predictions.

The job timed out because each fit_predict runs the nested base_predict 90 times, and each call refits a 200-tree random forest on about 2250 features plus a 9-config kernel-ridge grid search; I cut the forest to 100 trees with sqrt feature sampling and reduced the kernel-ridge grid to its single chosen config.

Adds one transductive self-training round at the end of fit_predict: test rows get their first-pass stack predictions as pseudo-labels (weight 0.3, real rows weight 1.0), the RF and LightGBM members are refit on the augmented set, the kernel member and meta-learner coefficients are kept, and a try/except falls back to first-pass predictions.

The job overran the 600 s limit because each of the 6 base_predict calls ran a 3x3 lambda/weight grid search with 4 inner folds (36 large kernel solves per call) on top of the RF and LightGBM fits. Fixing lam and wr at the grid's default values removes that search and should bring the 15 fits under the limit; the timing fix is not verified by a run.

Factorise the kernel-ridge training kernel once per RBF weight and inner fold with np.linalg.eigh, evaluate lambda in (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0) in closed form, and keep the summed-absolute-error selection and final np.linalg.solve refit.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access and no pasted values, and it does not use test labels. fit_predict still uses only train_y.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The candidate simplifies the model in two ways: it drops the inner GroupKFold grid search over (lam, wr) and fixes them at (0.3, 1.0), and it replaces the out-of-fold positive-Ridge stacking with a plain mean of the 3 base predictions. Both changes are legitimate. They are simpler and they score worse.

base_predict now gets groups=None. The removed grid search was the only place shown in the diff that used ga, and the job ran without crashing. The parts of base_predict not shown in the diff may still use groups, but the run did not crash. Leftover imports (Ridge, GroupKFold, MurckoScaffold) may now be unused, which is a minor cleanup point.

The numbers are consistent. Candidate 0.5271 vs incumbent 0.4895 is 0.0376 worse. With sd 0.0042 and one run each, the se of the difference is 0.0042*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00594, so z ≈ -6.33, which matches the harness value of -6.338. Rejecting is correct: tuning the hyperparameters and stacking the base models both matter.

description: The job exceeded 600 s because each fit_predict runs six base_predict calls (five nested stacking folds plus the final fit), and each call also runs a 12-decomposition eigh hyperparameter grid for the kernel ridge model; I remove the nested stacking in favor of an equal-weight average of the three base models and fix the kernel ridge hyperparameters to a single setting.

Replace the Ridge meta-learner with a non-negative, sum-to-one weight average fitted by minimising MAE on the out-of-fold base predictions (SLSQP, equal-weight start), and drop the now-unused Ridge import.

Train the stack's LightGBM member for 900 rounds with a learning rate that decays from 0.06 to 0.01 along a cosine curve, applied through lgb.reset_parameter as a callback, with all other LightGBM parameters unchanged.
